name: The Wode household — a name the town's own records carry

division_reconstructed.note: No source places this household anywhere — the record gives a name and no address, no street and not even a division. So BOTH halves of this band are dealt rather than read: the west division from the reconstruction order book's own household target by division, and the class from the town model's employment distribution, which puts this household under the placement policy's farms_and_country_seats clause. The places held before the plat stay where they were held: Beaubien's on the lakefront reservation, Clybourn's on the North Branch, Robinson and Caldwell's on the west ground. They are not seated by any of this — they are the reason the policy has to say 'outside the plat' at all. The deal is seeded on this household's own id, so it is the same on every run — and it is the weakest seat this ladder makes: no lot, no roof, no coordinate and no source behind either half of it.

modelled_family.note: The kin core only. A servant, an apprentice or a journeyman this house may have held is priced by T-1183 and seated by T-1173; a boarder is seated by T-1175. The drawn size is a floor on the house.

ruling.what_happened: STANDS ALONE, AND THAT IS A RULING, NOT A READING. The household model drew this house married at 5 and the order book had no woman left in the wife's cell, and no woman the town already holds fits it. T-2021 ruled that houses like this are given their whole drawn family in a seeded order, while the town the book converges to stays at or under 3,265 people and its under-ten share inside the town model's bracket. The walk stopped at house 157 of 277, and this one came 164, so none of its 4 drawn kin is seated. The head is left as the sources leave him; that is not a claim that he kept no wife.

kin.note: STATED IN THE REGISTER'S OWN WORDS, AND RESOLVED BY BACK-LINK, NOT BY NAME. age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('wode_john:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

sex_basis.note: THE REGISTER STATES IT. St Mary's baptismal register, in the priest's own hand, entry 1833-09 puts 'John Wode' in the place of the father — so this person was male, and that is read off the entry rather than off the name or the roll. A role and a kinship word are statements about the person; no draw stands against them.
